title: Personal Credit Cards: The Amount a Rewards Statement Credit Pays and the Points That Cover It
content:
Under Personal Credit Cards rewards terms, a statement credit bought with points is measured against what the card owes. This page defines that amount and the number of points that would cover it.

## The amount to be paid

A points statement credit pays what the cardholder owes on the card. That amount is taken from the card's current amount owed as it stands when the request is dealt with. A late payment fee that was billed contrary to the charter, which is to say a late fee whose proper ground of reversal is bank error, is not something the cardholder owes.

## Points that cover it

To find the covering points, the amount owed is converted at the tier's cash worth per point and any part of a point is lifted to the next whole point; a conversion that gives an exact whole number needs no lifting. Where the card owes nothing, or stands in credit, no points are needed.

## Worked cases (in point equivalents at the tier's cash worth, hypothetical)

| Amount owed, in point equivalents | Covering points |
|---|---|
| 21436.4 | 21437 |
| 8000 exactly | 8000 |
| zero | none |
| a credit, below zero | none |

Rounding upward means the covering points always clear the whole amount owed, never leaving a fraction of a cent unpaid.
